commits.message:
feat(reporting): expand dashboard to P0 report spec (ingestion, classification, AI dependency, review queue, signature quality)

Follow-up to the initial reporting dashboard, expanding it to match
the requested report catalog's P0 items and navigation (Overview |
Ingestion | Parser Quality | AI Usage & Cost | Recruitment Intelligence
| Sender Intelligence | Exceptions -- the last three stubbed as
"not built yet, P1" rather than faked with placeholder numbers).

Investigated the existing schema before writing anything new: Hermes
already instruments almost everything this needed --
intake_log (received/parsed/duplicate per message), field_provenance
(one row per extracted field, with extractor/method/confidence, plus a
second row with extractor='reviewer_correction' whenever a human fixes
one), and app/drafts/accuracy.py (already computes fill-rate/precision
for job-requirement and hotlist fields from those correction rows).
Nothing here needed new instrumentation -- it needed a reader.

The flagged P0 item -- signature parser quality, "don't just report
confidence, track confidence vs correctness" -- turned out to be a
direct extension of that existing accuracy engine: signature.py's
output already gets the SAME field_provenance treatment
(field_path="signature.<field>"), including the SAME human-correction
tracking. Extended app/drafts/accuracy.py's _field_accuracy_for_type
to accept draft_type=None (signature parsing runs regardless of
document kind, unlike job/hotlist fields which are scoped to one
draft_type), added SIGNATURE_FIELDS, and added false_positive_rate,
avg_stated_confidence, and calibration_gap (avg confidence minus
measured precision -- positive means Hermes is systematically MORE
confident than it turns out to be correct, the dangerous direction) to
every field's output.

Bug found and fixed while wiring this up: the first attempt showed 0%
fill rate for "name" and "company" -- the actual field_path keys
signature.py writes are full_name/first_name/last_name/company_name,
not name/company. Confirmed against the real contact dict keys in
field_provenance before finalizing the field list, catching this
before it shipped a report that silently missed the exact fields the
reported false-extraction incident was about.

Important caveat surfaced in the UI itself, not just this message: a
field with zero recorded corrections shows 100% precision, but that
can mean "genuinely always correct" OR "nobody has been correcting
it" -- those look identical from the data alone. Added a needs_spot_
check flag (high fill volume + low stated confidence + zero
corrections) and highlight it in the signature quality table, since
that combination is the pattern worth a human actually looking at
rather than trusting the 100%.

New app/reporting/service.py functions, all sharing the same read-only
contract as the existing ones: get_ingestion_health (received/parsed/
duplicate, processing rate, by channel), get_classification_report
(draft_type distribution + confidence + daily trend),
get_ai_dependency_report (parser-only vs AI-assisted % from
field_provenance.extractor, cost per 1,000 drafts), get_review_queue_
report (status counts + the SPECIFIC record-level reasons a draft
needs review -- company_missing, job_title_missing, etc., not just a
blanket low-confidence label), get_signature_quality_report, and
get_today_summary (the single top-of-dashboard KPI bar). All wired
into both GET /reports/overview and the assistant's tool registry, so
a chat question about ingestion/signature/AI-dependency gets answered
from the exact same functions the dashboard charts use.

Also fixed a second real bug caught while testing against production
data: get_ingestion_health's by_channel breakdown was summing every
intake_log status (received + parsed + duplicate) for the same
message, roughly doubling the real inbound volume. Now counts only
"received" rows. Covered by a regression test.

Frontend: ReportsPage.tsx restructured into the 7-tab navigation
above. New FieldAccuracyTable component (shared by future field-
accuracy reports) shows fill rate, precision, false-positive rate,
avg stated confidence, calibration gap, and correction counts per
field, with the spot-check flag highlighted.

New coverage in scripts/hermes-950-reporting-assistant-check.py (12
new checks): every new function's shape, the by-channel double-
counting regression test, AI-dependency percentages summing to 100%,
the signature report covering the exact fields from the reported
incident, and both new endpoints via the real FastAPI app. Verified
end-to-end against real production data throughout (not just the test
suite) -- including a live assistant question about signature parser
accuracy that correctly routed to the new tool and cited real
precision/false-positive numbers. Full regression suite run against a
fresh schema and freshly built image: hermes-950-reporting-assistant-
check.py passes all 20 checks; every other failure in the suite
reproduces identically against the current, unmodified production
image in the same throwaway harness (missing live server, missing
Langfuse/MS Graph credentials) -- confirmed pre-existing environment
gaps, not regressions from this change. Frontend type-checks and
builds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
